plan: [My signal is 35. Unconditional E[common]=24.5, but winning implies my signal is unusually high so the true common value is lower (winner's curse). Using the distribution (common 20–29, noise −20..20) and conditioning on my signal being the highest among three, E[common | I win] ≈ 23.96. Assuming symmetric play, bid this conditional expectation (rounded to $0.1) to maximize long-run expected profit.]

[My signal s=29 carries no information about the common value because noise is uniform over a range that makes P(s|C) constant; thus C|s is uniform on {20,...,29}. So expected true value E[C|s]=24.5. In a second-price auction, bidding the expected common value maximizes long-run profit and avoids winner's curse. I will bid 24.5.]

[Given my signal s=9, the prior for common value c is uniform on [20,29] and noise is uniform on [-20,20], so the likelihood is constant over [20,29]. Thus the posterior is uniform on [20,29], giving E[c|s]=24.5. In a second-price auction, bidding the expected common value conditional on my signal is the rational Bayes strategy to avoid the winner's curse and maximize expected profit. I will bid $24.5 (allowed in $0.1 increments).]
